audit.why: Difficulty HARD 8/10 fits: Ekko controls early trades with Timewinder/W zoning, TF plays for map post-6. Difficulty framing across early/mid/side/teamfight is consistent between layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart shows Ekko on all 7 rows; content win[] and packet levelChart both say Skill at Level 3, Levels 4-5 and 2+ items. The two layers render contradictory answers.
audit.why: Packet levelChart and content whys agree (roam threat offsets poke 3-5; late is flank-pick vs combo). Full layer carries a blanket side.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side, phases[3].side, phases[6].side moved to Skill with ratings 5/10 and whys rewritten to match; win[] already correct so no content edit needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no number; enemyWin was a template ('lands R, denies your pattern'); missing interactions: Phase Dive auto-reset as the burst tell, W anomaly shield/stun absorbing your burst, Chronobreak untargetability dodging your commit.
audit.why: Kit file: Chronobreak 110/80/50s, Parallel Convergence 22/20/18/16/14s, Phase Dive 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s with autoReset flag; R flags untargetable+heal; W flags shield+hardCC.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with real numbers; enemyWin grounded in the E-reset open, W anomaly stun and R rewind-out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both suspectNames are false positives: 'Gold Card' is TF's own W card (correct usage in spikes[1].text) and 'Parallel Convergence' in wants.foe[1] is Ekko's real W name.

edits.before: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus card cycling is a real short trade — but your game is the clock, not the lane.
edits.after: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus a card cycle answer his 9s Timewinder trades — the lane evens into a skill fight.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q the wave, lock cards on cooldown, and watch side lanes like they're your KDA.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — Q the wave, sidestep his placed W (22s early), and this window stays contestable.

edits.before: Late TF is a coin with two good sides: split the side lane R-safe, or hold Destiny as the pick-and-collapse button.
edits.after: Late it's your flank picks against his combo engage: split R-safe, or hold Destiny to catch him before he E-flanks in.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Check it before every step-up. - W gold card is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Chronobreak: 110s at rank 1, 50s at rank 3 — track the hologram and save your final damage for after the rewind. - Parallel Convergence runs 22s early: once his W is placed and burned, punish that long window. - Yellow card is the lifeline; hold it for his 9s Phase Dive.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Ekko wins by opening the Phase Dive auto-reset, stunning you inside his W anomaly, and rewinding out of whatever punish you planned.

edits.before: Lock gold off-screen, walk up once, card-auto-Q, and leave — one stun-chunk per cycle is all the lane asks of you.
edits.after: A freeze near your tower makes him step past river to trade — that's gold-card-plus-jungler territory; Q the far minions.

edits.before: Cycling cards inside his engage range for stacked-deck greed — TF dies in exactly one mistimed auto-walk per game; don't pre-book it.
edits.after: Plate greed with no yellow card up is Phase Dive bait — his E auto-reset closes the gap instantly; back off until Pick A Card is ready.
